title: raincloud manifest (sources.json)
description: JSON Schema for sources.json, the manifest that drives the raincloud pipeline. Companion to sources.schema.md (the human-friendly reference). Validated by `python -m scripts.pipeline.validate_manifest`. Note: `transform.handler` is intentionally not enum-constrained here — the validator cross-checks it against the live handler registry in scripts/pipeline/handlers/__init__.py so this schema doesn't need updating every time a handler is added.

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version. Bumping this would create outputs/v{n}/ alongside outputs/v1/. The within-version layout is outputs/v{n}/<slug>/<format>/<filename> (e.g. parquet/<slug>.parquet, vortex/<slug>.vortex).

notes.description: Free-form metadata about the manifest itself. Object or string.

slug.description: kebab-case identifier (a few legacy nyc-tlc slugs use snake_case); matches outputs/v{n}/<slug>/parquet/<slug>.parquet.

family.description: Curatorial grouping. Adding a new family is a deliberate choice — discuss before extending the enum.

kind.description: Reference type. `dataset_card` rarely needs a separate entry since `license.source_url` typically points there; reserve `references` for canonical paper / blog / homepage / source-repo links.

references.description: Optional canonical references for the dataset beyond `license.source_url`. Most useful for surfacing the underlying paper or the project homepage in the TUI.

spdx.description: SPDX id, or free-form token if no SPDX assignment exists. Describes the aggregator's declared license — see `scrape_advisory` for the gap between that and any uncleared underlying content.

scrape_advisory.description: Heavy asterisk for datasets that aggregate or reference content whose underlying licenses have not been individually cleared (public-web scrapes, Common Crawl derivatives, image/code corpora distributed under takedown models). When non-null, the text renders as a prominent warning in datasets.md, list_datasets --long, and the TUI. `spdx` still describes the aggregator's declared license; this field captures the gap between that and the unclaimed status of the underlying content.

urls.description: List of upstream URLs to fetch in order. May be empty when fetch.type="custom" and the handler resolves URLs at runtime (e.g. Public BI workloads).

requires_interactive_accept.description: Marks datasets gated behind a one-time terms-of-use click-through on the upstream's web UI. Valid on fetch.type=kaggle (Kaggle dataset ToS) and fetch.type=huggingface (HF gated repos like LAION). Both fetchers catch the 401/403 and surface a 'visit URL, click Accept, re-run' message regardless of this flag — setting it lets the orchestrator announce the requirement up front.

hf_allow_patterns.description: huggingface-only: glob patterns passed through to snapshot_download(allow_patterns=...). Lets a slug fetch a subset of a giant repo (e.g. just one config or sample of fineweb) without paying for the whole corpus. Null/omitted = whole repo.

hf_revision.description: huggingface-only: git revision (branch, tag, or commit SHA) passed through to snapshot_download(revision=...). Null/omitted = whatever main resolves to at fetch time.

options.description: Reader-specific kwargs. Shape varies by reader — see scripts/pipeline/parse.py.

handler.description: Name of a registered handler in scripts/pipeline/handlers/__init__.py. Validated by validate_manifest.py.

output.description: Output filename. Ignored for multi-output handlers — they emit per-output_slug filenames.

row_stability.description:
How the upstream row count evolves over time:
  static     — frozen snapshot (Kaggle dump, archived release, Wikipedia 2024 dump). expect.rows is contractual; drift is a bug.
  grow_only  — append-only live source (NYC OpenData, NOAA observations); past rows don't change.
  mutable    — past records may be revised or deleted (some live CKAN portals).
  null/absent — unclassified.

vortex_skip_reason.description: Free-form explanation of why the Vortex sibling is opted out. Required (non-null string) when vortex=false; must be null when vortex=true. Surfaced in docs/v{n}/vortex_skip.md, the TUI detail pane, and list_datasets --json. Use this for known type-support gaps in the current Vortex release (e.g. FixedSizeBinary(16) UUIDs, nested list<struct> on chunked-array writes) so the catalog records *why* a slug doesn't have a `.vortex` rather than leaving it ambiguous.

Hydrate.description: Opt-in hydration config. When non-null, the slug carries a URL column whose contents can be dereferenced into a sibling parquet at outputs/v{n}/<slug>/parquet-hydrated/<slug>.parquet. The base slug ships only the URL index — hydration is a separate, deliberately sketchy artefact tier with no file-size guarantees. Run `python -m scripts.pipeline.hydrate <slug>` to produce the hydrated copy.

url_column.description: Name of the existing string column whose values are URLs to dereference.

output_column.description: Name of the new column to add to the hydrated copy (typically `content` or `bytes`).

output_type.description: Wire shape of the dereferenced payload — `binary` for image/audio/PDF bytes, `string` for HTML/text. Embeddings or other model-derived representations belong on a sibling slug, not on this column.

advisory.description: Free-form per-slug warning describing the hydration's pitfalls — takedown rates, copyright posture, expected null-row prevalence. Rendered in HYDRATING.md alongside the global 'this dereferences arbitrary URLs' preamble.

blocked_hosts_extra.description: Optional per-slug list of hostnames to add to the hydrate stage's blocklist. Stacks on top of the user-supplied --block files and (if enabled) URLhaus. Use for slug-specific bans the dataset author wants to enforce regardless of run-time flags. Hostnames only — no schemes, no paths.
